$comment: Expected OUTCOMTS for the frozen CPS-0001 v1.0-RC1 test vectors - NOT rules.
precedence: Expected outcomes are derived from the normative CPS-0001 specification (repository root CPS0001.md). If this artifact conflicts with the normative specification, THE SPECIFICATION WINS.
independence: This oracle is derived solely from the normative specification, the JSON Schema, and the test vectors. It contains no reference to any implementation, SDK, CLI, reference verifier, conformance suite, test file, or datastore. An independent implementer can use it without consulting any MyShape source code.
evaluationTimeNote: Time-sensitive checks (V4 condition 2 'interval.end <= now' and V6 freshness) MUST be evaluated against this fixed verification time, not a live system clock, so that results are reproducible.

outcomeSemantics.PASS: The check was applied and the receipt satisfied it.
outcomeSemantics.FAIL: The check was applied and the receipt violated it.
outcomeSemantics.N/A: The check does not apply to this receipt. Permitted ONLY for V7 on a genesis receipt (previousReceiptHash === null). A non-genesis receipt whose predecessor cannot be resolved is NOT N/A - it is a V7 FAIL with PREDECESSOR_MISSING. N/A is not a failure.

verdictSemantics: Overall verdict is VALID when every applicable check passes, and INVALID when exactly one or more applicable checks fail.
checkOrderNote: This is the NORMATIVE evaluation order defined by the canonical CPS0001.md (Evaluation order and first-failure rule). V7 is evaluated after V2 and before V3-V6. The vector objects below list checks in this same order.
firstFailureRule: The reported failureCode is the failure code of the FIRST failing core check in checkOrder. A verifier may short-circuit at the first failure or may continue evaluating the remaining checks for diagnostics, but a later failure MUST NOT displace, override or replace the normative first-failure code. Within V7, the four receipt-to-receipt checks are evaluated in the numbered order 1-4 of the specification and the first that fails supplies the V7 code.
v7FailClosed: For a non-genesis receipt whose previousReceiptHash cannot be resolved to a predecessor in the trusted store, receipt-to-receipt continuity is NOT established: V7 = FAIL, failureCode = PREDECESSOR_MISSING, overall = INVALID. A verifier MUST NOT report N/A for such a receipt.
v7StoreNote: V7 requires a predecessor resolved from a trusted store. When a non-genesis receipt's previousReceiptHash cannot be resolved to a predecessor in the trusted store, V7 fails with the core failure code PREDECESSOR_MISSING (see v7FailClosed above). PREDECESSOR_MISSING is a member of the v1.0-RC1 core failure-code vocabulary: it is the normative V7 code for an unresolved predecessor, not merely an integration-layer diagnostic.

vectors.note: Genesis receipt (previousReceiptHash === null), so V7 is N/A and fail-closed does not apply.

Non-genesis receipt. V7 evaluated with test-vectors/valid/single-engine.json as the resolved predecessor: the predecessor resolves, so fail-closed does not apply, and all four protocol-core checks pass.

GENESIS receipt: previousReceiptHash is null, so V7 does not apply and is reported N/A. The fail-closed rule is scoped to non-genesis receipts and therefore does not apply here. The receipt is past expiresAt at the fixed evaluation time, so V6 fails and supplies the first-failure code. The stored directory name is historical packaging metadata, not a verdict.
Genesis receipt, structurally valid, expired before the fixed evaluation time. V7 is N/A, so V6 supplies the first failing check.
Genesis receipt whose declared payloadDigest does not match the recomputed digest of payload. V7 is N/A; the digest is inside the signed payload, so V5 is the first failing check.

Non-genesis receipt whose previousReceiptHash is a literal placeholder string rather than a digest of any receipt, so it cannot be resolved to a predecessor in the trusted store. V7 FAILS with PREDECESSOR_MISSING. The receipt is additionally past expiry at the fixed evaluation time, so V6 fails as well, but V7 precedes V6 in checkOrder and therefore sets the reported first-failure code.

N-2 dedicated predecessor fixture. GENESIS receipt (previousReceiptHash is null), so V7 is N/A and it is fully VALID. It is the resolved predecessor for the three N-2 V7 child vectors below; its JCS receipt hash is 9742df6972f96075772eb90af94adb638fb9a618634f6f7c764fb2777840fead. Shares issuer id n2-issuer-0001 and the N-2 public key with inconsistent-assertions, subject-mismatch and chain-temporal-violation; issuer-mismatch deliberately carries issuer id n2-issuer-0002 with the SAME public key, so that V7 check 3 is isolated as a pure issuer-identity-label test.

N-2 V3 negative vector. GENESIS receipt (previousReceiptHash is null), so V7 is N/A and the chain dimension is fully isolated. Claims continuityMaintained = true while observationOccurred = false, which is the single normative V3 failure condition. V3 precedes V4-V6, and V7 does not apply, so V3 supplies the first-failure code.

N-2 V7 check-2 negative vector. Non-genesis; previousReceiptHash resolves to test-vectors/valid/n2-predecessor.json. V7 check 1 (hash) passes, check 2 fails because this receipt's subject.id differs from the predecessor's, and checks 3 and 4 would pass. Exactly one V7 condition fails, so the reported code is SUBJECT_MISMATCH.

N-2 V7 check-3 negative vector. Non-genesis; previousReceiptHash resolves to test-vectors/valid/n2-predecessor.json. V7 checks 1 and 2 pass; check 3 fails because this receipt carries issuer id n2-issuer-0002 while the predecessor carries n2-issuer-0001. Both use the SAME public key, so the check isolates the issuer identity label and introduces no signing-key ambiguity. Exactly one V7 condition fails.

N-2 V7 check-4 negative vector. Non-genesis; previousReceiptHash resolves to test-vectors/valid/n2-predecessor.json. V7 checks 1, 2 and 3 pass; check 4 fails because predecessor.interval.end (2026-07-23T10:00:10Z) is later than this receipt's interval.start (2026-07-23T09:00:00Z). The receipt's own temporal consistency is intact: all five V4 conditions hold, and V7 precedes V4 in the normative order in any case. Exactly one V7 condition fails.

predecessorBindings.note: V7 requires the predecessor to be resolved from a trusted store. The bindings below are normative fixture wiring: each child's previousReceiptHash MUST equal SHA-256(JCS(predecessor)) for the predecessor file named here. A verifier that cannot resolve these bindings will, correctly, report PREDECESSOR_MISSING instead of the expected failure code. This mapping is public and must not be left implicit.
predecessorBindings.howToCompute: predecessorHash = SHA-256( UTF-8( JCS(predecessor receipt JSON) ) ), where JCS is RFC 8785 canonical JSON: object keys sorted ascending by UTF-16 code unit, no insignificant whitespace, null preserved, numbers in ECMAScript Number-toString form, strings escaped per JSON. See CPS0001 Annex N-2.

coverageGap.issue: No remaining negative-coverage gap. The V3 rule and four of the five protocol-core V7 failure codes are now exercised by published fixtures.
coverageGap.covered: INCONSISTENT_ASSERTIONS by test-vectors/invalid/inconsistent-assertions.json. PREDECESSOR_MISSING by test-vectors/invalid/broken-chain.json via the unresolvable-predecessor path. SUBJECT_MISMATCH, ISSUER_MISMATCH and TEMPORAL_VIOLATION by the three N-2 child vectors resolved against test-vectors/valid/n2-predecessor.json. V7 check 1 is additionally exercised as a PASS by test-vectors/valid/multi-engine.json and by all three N-2 child vectors.
coverageGap.stillAbsent: A V7 check-1 FAIL (CHAIN_BROKEN) in which the predecessor resolves but its JCS hash does not equal the pointer is not constructible as a receipt fixture: the predecessor is resolved BY that pointer, so a mismatch would require a store integrity failure rather than a receipt property. Retained as P2. test-vectors/valid/agent-trace.json does NOT exercise the unresolvable-predecessor path: it is a genesis receipt (previousReceiptHash is null), so its V7 is N/A.
coverageGap.notApplicable: None. All resolvable V7 failure codes are exercised by published fixtures; only the check-1 CHAIN_BROKEN gap above remains (P2).
